_meta.project: instex TELESCOPES mode -- Hubble Space Telescope Optical Telescope Assembly (OTA): optics, the single f/24 Cassegrain focus and how the instruments share it, and the entrance pupil
_meta.companion: data/telescopes/hst.md (same content as Markdown tables). Reuses data/imaging/hst.json (block 'hst_ota') by key: the source keys OTAHB, L12, PRIMOTA, TT63, TTACS, TTUVIS, TTIR, WFC3IHB, ACSIHB and ISR0814 are the same documents under rawdata/imaging/; entries that restate an imaging value carry 'imaging_key' (a path into data/imaging/hst.json). New documents are saved unmodified under rawdata/telescopes/hst/.
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short verbatim quote from the saved document. derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). value null = not published in the sources found. Quotes were machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text (pdftotext -layout, -raw and default reading order, per page; HTML with tags stripped; the Tiny Tim plain-text tables) after glyph/whitespace normalisation. Figure labels without a text layer carry check 'ocr' (found in tesseract OCR of the figure rendered at 300-600 dpi) or 'figure' (read visually, not machine-checkable).
_meta.quote_normalisation: NFKC; curly quotes, primes and double primes, en/em dashes, minus signs, the multiplication sign (x), micro/mu (u) normalised; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces; table rows quoted as whitespace-separated cells; matching also tried with line-break hyphens removed and with all whitespace removed. OCR typos of the scanned 1990 OTA Handbook are kept verbatim (e.g. 'Chretian', 'baffie', 'Seconday', 'WFfPC', 'milliarseconds'); the Lallo 2012 text layer renders micro as '#', arcsec as '!' and f-prime as 'f !'.
_meta.page_conventions: OTAHB printed page = PDF page - 6; FGSIHB and the STScI Cycle-34 handbooks printed page = PDF page - 1; Lallo 2012 cited by arXiv PDF page; NASA SM3B Media Guide sections cited by printed page (1-N, 5-N = PDF page N of the section file).
_meta.coordinates: V1 = optical axis (positive toward the aperture door), V2 parallel to the solar-array drive axis, V3 toward the nominal Sun direction (OTAHB Sec. 1.3.1.3). Current STScI documents use U1 = V1, U2 = -V2, U3 = -V3 (PRIMSYS). Focal-plane aperture positions are given as projected on the sky (arcsec); 'the cassegrain telescope inverts the image of the sky onto the focal plane' (OTAHB p. 20). Pupil azimuths here are measured from +V3 toward +V2 in the plane of OTAHB Figure 4.1 (+V3 drawn up, +V2 drawn right); whether that figure (and the Tiny Tim pad table) is viewed from the sky or from the focal plane is not stated.

telescope.name: Hubble Space Telescope -- Optical Telescope Assembly (OTA)
telescope.recommended_preset: Two-mirror Ritchey-Chretien Cassegrain. Primary: 2400 mm, concave hyperboloid, R = 11040 mm, f1 = 5520 mm (f/2.3), K1 = -1.0022985 by design (as built -1.0132 to -1.0144: the famous spherical aberration, ~1/2 wave, 253-277 nm rms wavefront, surface error ~2.3 um at the edge; MG5: the edge was 'too flat' by about 2 um), 600 mm central hole. Secondary: convex hyperboloid, R = -1358 mm, K2 = -1.49686, 281 mm diameter (310 mm with housing), 4906.071 mm in front of the primary, magnification 10.435. One focus: f/24 Cassegrain, f = 57.6 m, 3.58 arcsec/mm, 1500.129 mm behind the primary vertex (6406.200 mm behind the secondary); usable field ~28 arcmin = 0.46 m diameter (focal-surface fits out to 14 arcmin radius); curved focal surface (sag 43.5 mm at 14 arcmin, DERIVED radius ~650 mm). The field is shared spatially: 4 axial bays (ACS, COS, STIS, NICMOS) take light directly a few arcmin off axis; 4 radial bays take light via pick-off mirrors -- WFC3 through a flat 45-deg pick-off at the field centre, and the 3 FGSs through pickle-shaped plane pick-offs covering quarter annuli 10-14 arcmin from the axis (~69 arcmin2 each). Reflections before an instrument's own optics: 2 for an axial bay, 3 for a radial bay (DERIVED). Pupil: 2400 mm circle, central obscuration radius 396.0 mm (eps = 0.330, the secondary baffle), 4 spider vanes 25.654 mm wide along +-V2 and +-V3, 3 primary-mirror pads of diameter 150.368 mm (Figure 4.1; Tiny Tim 156 mm) near 0.89 of the radius.

primary.spherical_aberration: rms wavefront 253-277 nm (~1/2 wave); edge ~2.3 um (L12) / ~2 um (MG5) too flat

fgs_field.derived: DERIVED: annular sector area (84.15/360) x pi x (14^2 - 10^2) = 70.5 arcmin2 (inner radius 10.2: 67.5 arcmin2); three FGSs = 3 x 69 = 207 arcmin2, 34% of the pi x 14^2 = 616 arcmin2 field. In the focal plane 10-14 arcmin = 167-233 mm from the axis (OTAHB Table 2.7: 10 arcmin ~ 167 mm interpolated between the 9 and 11 arcmin rows, 14 arcmin = 233.2 mm).

pupil.summary: Entrance pupil = the 2400 mm primary, with a central obscuration of radius 396.0 mm (eps = 0.330; the secondary baffle), a 4-vane cross spider 25.654 mm wide along the V2 and V3 axes (vanes run from 396.0 mm to the rim, 804.0 mm long), and 3 primary-mirror pads (circles 150.368 mm across, one on the +V3 vane at 1066.8 mm, two at 1071.88 mm). Tiny Tim models the same features with slightly different numbers (spider 0.022, pads 0.065 of the radius at ~0.89). The pads also cause a trefoil wavefront term (L12).

spider.derived: DERIVED: 25.654/1200 = 0.0214 of the radius; 804.0 = 1200 - 396.0 (vane from obscuration edge to rim); vane area 4 x 25.654 x 804.0 mm2 = 825.0 cm2

Alignment of diffraction spikes in OTA PSF

spider.note: Vane count and the cross orientation are visual from Figure 4.1 (vanes drawn on the +V3, -V3, +V2 and -V2 axes); no text statement of the count was found. The secondary is held by the spider (OTAHB p. 34: "the secondary mirror spiders").

pads.derived: DERIVED: az = 180 - 58.5 = 121.5 deg and 180 + 67.6 = 247.6 deg; radii 0.889 and 0.893 of 1200 mm; pad radius 75.18 mm = 0.0627 of the pupil radius. Area check: vanes 825.0 + pads 3 x pi x 7.518^2 = 532.7 - pad/vane overlap 38.4 = 1319.4 cm2 vs the published 1320 cm2 for "pad supports and ... spider supports" (OTAHB p. 29): the Figure 4.1 dimensions reproduce the text.

Area with Tiny Tim numbers: 849.0 + 573.4 - 41.0 = 1381 cm2 (vs 1320 published).

alternatives.quote: the remainder of which is predominantly due to trefoil aberration coming from three primary mirror support pads
Superimposed on this pattern are spider diffraction spikes and a ripple effect caused· by the pads.

pads.note: Pad positions are hand-lettered dimensions read visually and confirmed by OCR (the 150.368 mm diameter OCRs as '50.368' with the leading 1 read as a quote mark; 58.5 OCRs as '585°'; 67.6 OCRs as '67.6 °' on one crop and '616°' on another). The +V3 pad overlaps its vane (hatched in the figure, visual). The figure is not drawn to scale (both lower pads are drawn at ~57-59 deg from -V3 despite the 67.6 label).

Size and position (distance ahead of the focus) of the WFC3 45-deg pick-off mirror and of the three FGS pick-off mirrors; the FGS pick-offs are described only by the arcmin field they cut out.
The number of reflections for axial and radial bays is not stated anywhere found; 2 and 3 are DERIVED from the bay descriptions.
Which way each radial bay points (in V2/V3) is not stated in text.
Whether OTAHB Figure 4.1 and the Tiny Tim pad table show the pupil as seen from the sky or from the focal plane.
A current (post-2009) statement of the clear (obscured) collecting area; the 38990 cm2 clear aperture is the 1990 handbook value.
An unvignetted-field specification for the f/24 focus (only ~28 arcmin / 0.46 m and the 14-arcmin focal-surface fits).
NICMOS status after 2012 and its aperture position (not in the Cycle-34 primer table).
conflicts: Mirror spacing: 4906.071 mm (OTAHB Table 2.1, design) vs 4906.9 mm (L12 Table 1). The on-orbit spacing is trimmed by secondary moves (L12).
Primary focal ratio: f/2.3 (L12; DERIVED 5520/2400 = 2.30) vs f/2.35 (MG5 p. 5-18).
Secondary diameter: 281 mm mirror, 310 mm with housing (L12 Table 1); 0.31 m (L12 Fig. 3); 12.2 in = 310 mm (MG1); 12 in (MG5). The media guides quote the housed size.
System focal length: 57.6 m (OTAHB, L12, MG5 '189 feet (57.6 m)') vs MG1 Fig. 1-4 '189 ft (56.7 m) folded to 21 ft (6.3 m)' -- a digit transposition in MG1 (189 ft = 57.6 m; 21 ft = 6.4 m as in MG5).
Focus behind the primary: 1500.129 mm (OTAHB Table 2.1), 'almost five feet' (OTAHB p. 13), 1.5 m (L12 Fig. 3) vs MG5 '3.3 feet (1.5 m)' (3.3 ft = 1.0 m; the metric value is the consistent one).

Exit pupil label in OTAHB Figure 2.4: the scan's text layer reads 'O.396M', the image and tesseract read 0.596 m; Table 2.1 (7003.51 - 6406.200 = 597.3 mm) and the mirror equation (596.5 mm) support 0.596 m.

FGS field: quarter annulus 10-14 arcmin, ~69 arcmin2, arcs 83.3/85 deg (FGSIHB Secs. 1.4.5, 2.6.1) vs inner radius 10.2 arcmin (FGSIHB glossary) vs '60 arcmin2 of field in a 90-degree sector' (MG5, 2002); PRIMSYS says '10 to 14 arcseconds' (unit typo for arcminutes).
Spider width: 25.654 mm (OTAHB Figure 4.1; 0.0214 R) vs 0.022 R = 26.4 mm (Tiny Tim) -- as in data/imaging/hst.json.

Pads: OTAHB Figure 4.1 (centres at 1066.8 mm on +V3 and 1071.88 mm for the other two; 58.5 deg and 67.6 deg from -V3; diameter 150.368 mm) vs Tiny Tim (0.8921/0.8853/0.8870 R = 1070.5/1062.4/1064.4 mm; 58.6 and 59.0 deg from -V3; diameter 0.13 R = 156 mm). The largest difference is the -V2-side pad azimuth (247.6 vs 239.0 deg). The Figure 4.1 numbers reproduce the published 1320 cm2 spider+pad area (1319.4 cm2 DERIVED); the Tiny Tim numbers give 1381 cm2.
Central obscuration naming: Tiny Tim labels 0.330 'OTA Secondary Mirror Radius'; the OTA Handbook calls it the secondary baffle obscuration, and the secondary mirror itself is 0.117-0.129 of D.

Spherical aberration size: rms 253-277 nm and edge error ~2.3 um (L12 p. 14), '256 nm' (L12 p. 10), 'about 2 microns' at the edge (MG5), 'about one-half wave' (PRIMOTA), '~1/2 wave' (WFC3IHB). Consistent at the level quoted; context only.
Bay history (not used for values): L12 Table 2 says GHRS was 'replaced with NICMOS' and FOS 'replaced with STIS', while L12 Figure 9 draws STIS where GHRS was and NICMOS where FOS was.
notes: There is one focus. Every instrument, including the guiders, sees the same f/24 beam; they are separated by position in the field, not by switching foci. Parallel observations with several instruments exploit this (L12 p. 29: 'the spatial sharing of the HST focal plane among the SIs').
Field angle to focal-plane radius (OTAHB Table 2.7): 1 arcmin = 16.758 mm, 5 arcmin = 83.73 mm, 10 arcmin ~ 167 mm (DERIVED between 9 and 11 arcmin rows), 14 arcmin = 233.24 mm.
Coordinate conventions: V2 = -U2, V3 = -U3 (PRIMSYS: 'V1=U1, V2= –U2 and V3= –U3').
